subject.title: Unhandled socket error in SSRF fetch wrapper can kill the gateway process (IPv6-only DNS + Happy Eyeballs)

question: Should maintainers accept a connector-layer SSRF socket-error fix for this issue once it preserves proxy pinning and has live or diagnostic proof, or require a different design before merge?
rationale: The fix touches OpenClaw's SSRF network security boundary, and the current linked PR has already been flagged for proof and proxy-pinning concerns that automation should not settle as product intent.

options.title: Require repaired shared SSRF fix
options.body: Have the linked PR or a narrow replacement handle socket errors in the shared dispatcher path, preserve pinned DNS/proxy behavior, and include live or diagnostic proof before landing.

options.title: Wait for live repro first
options.body: Keep this issue open and require IPv6-only no-route logs or Crabbox proof before accepting any code change to the SSRF boundary.

options.title: Close the linked PR and sponsor replacement
options.body: If the current PR remains unsafe, close it separately and use a maintainer-owned replacement patch for the same issue.

recommendation.title: Require repaired shared SSRF fix
recommendation.body: Have the linked PR or a narrow replacement handle socket errors in the shared dispatcher path, preserve pinned DNS/proxy behavior, and include live or diagnostic proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: History ties steipete to the explicit-proxy SSRF pinning and dispatcher-layer design that this fix must preserve.
